atoms.a: Can you find the Equator line on the globe?

feedback.end: Great! The Equator goes around the centre of the Earth, and doesn’t tilt very far towards or away from the Sun.

instruction.text: What do you think it means if the area around the Equator tilts less? Fill in the gaps.

atoms.b: The temperature for countries on the Equator tends to change ((much_more ++much_less)), and the weather is ((very_different ++mostly_the_same)) all year.

feedback.end: Instead of summer and winter, countries around the Equator normally have a rainy and a dry season.

instruction.text: Find the storm clouds in this image to learn about seasons in Jamaica.

end.text: Jamaica is close enough to the Equator that it stays the same temperature all year round. It is normally about 30°C every day of the year.
end.sound: Jamaica is close enough to the Equator that it stays the same temperature all year round. It is normally about 30 degrees Celsius every day of the year.

instruction.text: Match the images to the correct seasons.

feedback.finish: In Jamaica, June to November is rainy season. December to May is dry season.

instruction.text: Find the river in this image to learn about seasons in the Amazon rainforest.

end.text: The Amazon is on the Equator and has a rainy season and a dry season. However, it also gets plenty of rain during the dry season - that’s why it’s called a <u>rain</u>forest!

atoms.a: Jamaica has a rainy season and a dry season.
Jamaica tilts towards and away from the Sun a lot.
The Amazon rainforest still gets wet weather during its dry season.
